scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports total network loss: they
cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2), and they cannot even ping their own
gateway 195.11.14.1. pc1's own NIC still shows link up. The
partner AS is healthy internally: pc2 reaches its gateway
200.1.1.1 fine. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the LAN interface (eth1) toward pc1 on router1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth1 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 eth1 (195.11.14.1/24, the LAN
  interface toward pc1)
Mechanism: router1's eth1 is DOWN, so pc1's only gateway address
  195.11.14.1 is gone from the segment -- pc1 cannot even ARP its
  gateway and loses all off-host connectivity. On router1 the
  connected route 195.11.14.0/24 disappears from the RIB, so the
  `network 195.11.14.0/24` statement has no matching route and
  the prefix is withdrawn from BGP -- AS 2 also loses its path to
  pc1. pc1's own NIC still shows link up (its side of the virtual
  segment is unaffected), which is why a host-side check looks
  clean. The inter-AS link and the eBGP session machinery are not
  the fault; the failure sits on the router1<->pc1 LAN leg.
Localization: router1
Root cause: router1 eth1 (LAN link to pc1) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth1 up` on router1
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth1 up` on router1. The gateway 195.11.14.1 comes back on the
segment, the connected route returns and BGP re-advertises 195.11.14.0/24
automatically; pc1 reaches pc2 normally. pc1 needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: eth1 (the 195.11.14.0/24 LAN interface toward pc1) is down
must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: pc1 cannot even reach its gateway, so the fault is on the pc1<->router1 LAN leg, not the inter-AS link or the BGP session
bonus-rules-out-host: notes pc1's own link/IP/route are intact; the failure is on router1's side of the segment

line.command: ip -br link show eth1 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
router1's LAN-facing interface eth1 is administratively down at the Linux
kernel level. The interface has the IP address 195.11.14.1/24 assigned but
the link flags are <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> — no UP, no LOWER_UP — meaning the
OS never activated the interface (it was either shut down explicitly with
"ip link set eth1 down" or was simply never brought up in the startup
configuration). Because the interface is down, the kernel never installs a
connected route for 195.11.14.0/24, and ARP is suppressed on the segment.
When pc1 sends an ARP request for its default gateway 195.11.14.1, router1
drops it silently; pc1 therefore cannot resolve the gateway MAC address and
every outbound packet is stuck on-link — explaining the total loss reported.
The BGP session on eth0 (193.10.11.0/24) is unaffected and router2 is
healthy, which matches the report that pc2 and its gateway are fine. The
FRR configuration on router1 is correct (BGP AS 1, network 195.11.14.0/24,
peer 193.10.11.2) — the fault is purely at the OS interface layer.
Root cause: router1 eth1 was never brought up, cutting pc1 off from its
gateway.
Fix: on router1 run "ip link set eth1 up" to immediately restore the link;
make it permanent by adding "auto eth1 / iface eth1 inet static / address
195.11.14.1/24" to /etc/network/interfaces (or the equivalent Kathara
startup script) so eth1 comes up on every lab start.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names router1 as the affected device (router1 eth1) and attributes the failure to that interface.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies router1's eth1 (the 195.11.14.0/24 LAN interface toward pc1) as down and as the root cause.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: pc1 cannot even reach its gateway, so the fault is on the pc1<->router1 LAN leg, not the inter-AS link or the BGP session
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly locates the failure on router1's eth1 (LAN leg), explains pc1's inability to ARP its gateway, and notes the eBGP/session on the inter‑AS link is unaffected, satisfying the required distinction.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-host: notes pc1's own link/IP/route are intact; the failure is on router1's side of the segment
per_axis.rationale: The writeup blames router1 eth1 but does not explicitly state that pc1's NIC/link/IP/route are intact (it only implies ARP was sent), so it fails to clearly rule out the host side.
The agent explicitly instructs to run 'ip link set eth1 up' to restore connectivity and to make the change persistent in the startup config, which matches the expected fix.

Overall the diagnostic is well-grounded and causally coherent with adequate coverage.
